The famous ship that sank in 1912 after hitting an iceberg is the **RMS Titanic**.

To help you understand the complex concepts of blockchain technology described in your text, here are some analogies:

**1. The Digital Ledger as a Shared Notebook**
Imagine a group of friends who want to keep track of who owes whom money. Instead of one person holding the only notebook (which could be lost, stolen, or altered secretly), everyone in the group has their own identical notebook. Every time a transaction happens, everyone writes it down in their own book at the same time. This is like the "ledger copied across a thousand different computers."

**2. Immutability as Permanent Ink**
In a regular notebook, you might use a pencil and erase mistakes. In blockchain, it’s like using permanent marker. Once a transaction is written down and agreed upon by the group, it cannot be erased or changed. If you try to change your copy of the notebook, everyone else will see that your version doesn’t match theirs, and they will reject your change. This makes the record "immutable" (unchangeable).

**3. Decentralization and Verification as a Group Vote**
If one person tries to cheat by adding a fake entry to their notebook, the other 999 people will check their own notebooks. Since the majority didn’t agree to that fake entry, they will ignore it. The system only accepts changes that are "verified and agreed upon by the majority." This collective agreement process is what makes the system "extremely secure and trustworthy" because no single person or computer controls the truth.
